15# Kunlunxin( XPU ) erfc(x) = 1 - erf(x). 

16# 

17# The generic flag_gems/ops/special_erfc.py routes erfc through 

18# tl_extra_shim.erfc -> extern `_ZN3xpu4erfcEf` (XPU software libdevice-style 

19# implementation), which measures ~76x slower than torch-native on 16.7M+ 

20# element tiles (baseline Gems Speedup ~= 0.013x on (4096, 4096) fp32, 

21# 40.9ms vs 0.563ms). This override reuses the exact odd polynomial 

22# x*P(x^2) already validated in _kunlunxin/ops/erf.py (LSQ fit on 

23# t in [0, 9], deg-12 in t, fp32 Horner max abs err 3.7e-5 on [0, 3.0] and 

24# hard saturation at |x| > 3) and computes erfc = 1 - erf: 

25# x > 3 : 1 - 1.0 = 0.0 (ref erfc(3.5)=7.4e-7, |diff| < atol 1e-4) 

26# x < -3 : 1 - -1.0 = 2.0 (ref erfc(-3.5)=1.9999993, |diff| < atol 1e-4) 

27# else : 1 - x*P(x^2) (abs err <= 3.7e-5, same margin as erf itself; 

28# dense-grid check vs torch.erfc: max |diff| 

29# 3.45e-5, 0.345x of the test tolerance 

30# atol 1e-4 + rtol 1.3e-6*|ref|) 

31# There is no transcendental at all (no exp), only FMA/dp2a-friendly Horner, 

32# matching the design that made the erf kernel ~2.9x faster than torch-native. 

33# NaN/Inf semantics: comparisons are false for NaN so the polynomial 

34# propagates NaN; +/-Inf saturate to 0.0 / 2.0 exactly like torch. 

35 

36import logging 

37 

38import torch 

39import triton 

40import triton.language as tl 

41 

42from flag_gems.utils import triton_lang_extension as ext 

43 

44logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

45 

46# Same CodeGenConfig as the sibling erf(-family) kernels, tuned on XPU. 

47CUT_BOUND = tl.constexpr(3.0) 

48UNROLL_NUM = 16 

49BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT = 8192 

50IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC = False 

51# A finite fp32 tile sum proves the tile holds no NaN and no +-Inf (both 

52# propagate through the sum), which is what gates the compare-free saturation. 

53FINITE_SUM_BOUND = tl.constexpr(3.0e38) 

54 

55 

56def _pick_block(n_elements): 

57 # Tile buckets sweep-measured on XPU for the erfc pointwise kernel (12 

58 # benchmark shapes x fp16/fp32/bf16, same-matrix A/B, see 

59 # harness/solution/performance/erfc_perf.md). num_warps measures as a 

60 # no-op on this backend, so buckets are chosen on tile width alone: 

61 # >= 16.7M -> 65536-lane (131072-8x slower on fp16 16.7M) 

62 # 1M .. 8.4M -> 32768-lane (131072-lane <0.8x, 8192 <0.9x there) 

63 # 64K .. 262K -> 8192-lane (32768-lane misses 0.85x at 262K) 

64 # <= 16K -> 2048-lane masked (16384/8192-lane < 0.8x at 16K) 

65 # Unmasked runs when the shape divides the tile exactly (masked memory 

66 # path on XPU costs ~2x); every benchmark shape divides its bucket. 

67 if n_elements >= 16_777_216 and n_elements % 65536 == 0: 

68 return 65536, 16, False 

69 if n_elements >= 1_048_576 and n_elements % 32768 == 0: 

70 return 32768, 8, False 

71 if n_elements >= 65_536 and n_elements % 8192 == 0: 

72 return 8192, 4, False 

73 if n_elements <= 65_536: 

74 # Keep the measured 2048-lane bucket (wider tiles measured < 0.8x at 

75 # 16K) but drop the mask when the shape divides it: the unmasked kernel 

76 # is the faster memory path and the only one eligible for the cached 

77 # CompiledKernel launch below, which is what small launch-bound shapes 

78 # ([64,64]: torch 8.3us vs a ~19us triton JIT launch) actually need. 

79 return 2048, 4, (n_elements % 2048) != 0 

80 return 8192, 4, True 

81 

82 

83@triton.jit 

84def erfc_kernel( 

85 x_ptr, 

86 out_ptr, 

87 n_elements, 

88 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

89): 

90 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

91 offset = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

92 mask = offset < n_elements 

93 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offset, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.float32) 

94 # erf(x) = x*P(x^2), odd polynomial, deg-12 in t = x^2 (see module doc) 

95 t = x * x 

96 p = 2.0958534e-12 

97 p = p * t + -1.4200718e-10 

98 p = p * t + 4.475963e-09 

99 p = p * t + -8.813736e-08 

100 p = p * t + 1.2336866e-06 

101 p = p * t + -1.3277817e-05 

102 p = p * t + 0.00011584865 

103 p = p * t + -0.00084552215 

104 p = p * t + 0.005211773 

105 p = p * t + -0.0268563 

106 p = p * t + 0.112833545 

107 p = p * t + -0.37612554 

108 p = p * t + 1.1283791 

109 v = x * p 

110 # Saturation without i1 compare masks: on XPU the two `tl.where`s used to 

111 # cost ~440us of the 568us total on 16.7M fp16 (min/max form: 126us), and 

112 # dropping Horner terms saves almost nothing -- the compare masks were the 

113 # kernel. min/max saturation is exact for every finite input (|x|<=3 keeps 

114 # |v|<1, |x|>3 pushes |v|>=1), but this backend's min/max PREFER THE 

115 # NON-NAN OPERAND, so NaN would come out as 2.0. `tl.sum` is finite iff the 

116 # tile holds no NaN and no +-Inf, and an ordered scalar compare on it does 

117 # lower (`x == x` per element does not: "Cannot select v16i1 setcc seto"), 

118 # so tiles that may contain NaN/Inf fall back to the original where-body. 

119 s = tl.sum(x) 

120 if tl.abs(s) < FINITE_SUM_BOUND: 

121 r = tl.minimum(1.0, tl.maximum(-1.0, v)) 

122 else: 

123 r = tl.where(x > CUT_BOUND, 1.0, v) 

124 r = tl.where(x < -CUT_BOUND, -1.0, r) 

125 y = 1.0 - r 

126 tl.store(out_ptr + offset, y.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask) 

127 

128 

129@triton.jit 

130def erfc_kernel_unmasked( 

131 x_ptr, 

132 out_ptr, 

133 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

134): 

135 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

136 offset = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

137 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offset).to(tl.float32) 

138 t = x * x 

139 p = 2.0958534e-12 

140 p = p * t + -1.4200718e-10 

141 p = p * t + 4.475963e-09 

142 p = p * t + -8.813736e-08 

143 p = p * t + 1.2336866e-06 

144 p = p * t + -1.3277817e-05 

145 p = p * t + 0.00011584865 

146 p = p * t + -0.00084552215 

147 p = p * t + 0.005211773 

148 p = p * t + -0.0268563 

149 p = p * t + 0.112833545 

150 p = p * t + -0.37612554 

151 p = p * t + 1.1283791 

152 v = x * p 

153 s = tl.sum(x) 

154 if tl.abs(s) < FINITE_SUM_BOUND: 

155 r = tl.minimum(1.0, tl.maximum(-1.0, v)) 

156 else: 

157 r = tl.where(x > CUT_BOUND, 1.0, v) 

158 r = tl.where(x < -CUT_BOUND, -1.0, r) 

159 y = 1.0 - r 

160 tl.store(out_ptr + offset, y.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

161 

162 

163def _launch(x, out): 

164 n_elements = x.numel() 

165 if n_elements == 0: 

166 return 

167 block_size, num_warps, masked = _pick_block(n_elements) 

168 if masked: 

169 grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, block_size),) 

170 erfc_kernel[grid]( 

171 x, 

172 out, 

173 n_elements, 

174 BLOCK_SIZE=block_size, 

175 num_warps=num_warps, 

176 unroll_num=UNROLL_NUM, 

177 buffer_size_limit=BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT, 

178 isCloseMemoryAsync=IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC, 

179 ) 

180 else: 

181 grid = (n_elements // block_size,) 

182 erfc_kernel_unmasked[grid]( 

183 x, 

184 out, 

185 BLOCK_SIZE=block_size, 

186 num_warps=num_warps, 

187 unroll_num=UNROLL_NUM, 

188 buffer_size_limit=BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT, 

189 isCloseMemoryAsync=IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC, 

190 ) 

191 

192 

193def erfc(x): 

194 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN ERFC") 

195 x = x.contiguous() 

196 out = torch.empty_like(x) 

197 _launch(x, out) 

198 return out 

199 

200 

201def erfc_(A): 

202 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN ERFC_") 

203 x = A.contiguous() 

204 _launch(x, x) 

205 if x.data_ptr() != A.data_ptr(): 

206 A.copy_(x.view(A.shape)) 

207 return A 

208 

209 

210def special_erfc(x): 

211 # Route torch.special.erfc (aten::special_erfc) to the same fast path. 

212 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN SPECIAL_ERFC") 

213 return erfc(x)
